newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gencor plans international gold arm.
newsitem.headline: Gencor plans international gold arm.

text.p: South African mining house Gencor plans to build over the next five years an international gold company from offshore operations and exploration.

Unveiling the plans, Gencor stated its corporate mandate: "To create a fully integrated international mining company with one million ounces of annual gold production and a world class portfolio of development and exploration assets by 2001."
Gencor said the new division's market capitalisation could be five billion rand and it would have a reserve base equal to Gencor's existing South African gold arm Gengold.
The company is also likely to be listed on either the Toronto or London stock exchange.

The strategy to develop the new company would involve assembling a portfolio of major gold projects with the help of Canadian junior mining company Eldorado Gold Corporation, of which Gencor owns 40 percent.
Eldorado would assist in developing the smaller projects while Gencor would handle the large ones.
Once the portfolio was assembled as a balanced package, it would be floated as the Gencor gold investment vehicle.
"This would provide an attractive and unusual international pure gold investment play," Gencor said.
